title: Whatever else is unsure in this stinking dunghill of a world a mother’s love is not. Your mother brings you into the world, carries you first in her body. What do we know about what she feels? But whatever she feels, it, at least, must be real. It must be.
html_source:
Cranly vehemently believes in the importance and reality of a mother’s love. Everything else to him is nebulous.

He doesn’t claim to understand what mothers feel, but he is sure that their love exists.
